newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra denies report on rate cut delay.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra denies report on rate cut delay.

text.p: The office of Australian Finance Minister John Fahey on Tuesday denied he told a news agency that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) would wait for a decision on union wage claims before making any move on interest rates.
"That's not correct," the spokesman told Reuters when asked if the report was accurate.
The report on Monday night said Fahey had said in Switzerland that he expected the RBA to wait for a decision on a national union wage claim before deciding whether interest rates should be changed.

However, Fahey's spokesman said the minister had responded to a question about the bank by giving a list of economic indicators that its board was likely to consider when making a decision on interest rates.

He said that list included the Australian Council of Trade Unions' (ACTU) wage claim, but pointed out that the Reserve Bank itself had previously said that interest rate decisions were likely to take wage movements into account.
"It was in no means a suggestion that they should wait, or could wait, or might wait," the spokesman said.

"It was purely and simply a list of the indicators that are currently before us and obviously also the Reserve Bank in terms of any decisions the Reserve Bank might independently take," the spokesman said.
The Reserve Bank board is meeting on Tuesday to consider any further changes to monetary policy.
